page: Microsoft Azure M8-2ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. A defining characteristic of this server is its massive memory capacity of 219.0 GB, yielding 109.38 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, it includes 262 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate a significant performance tradeoff, as the server exhibits limited compute and memory throughput capabilities despite its large memory footprint. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores fall into the bottom 10% tier at 1031.38 and 1354.57 respectively. Similarly, Geekbench scores are low, with a single-core score of 878.0 and a multi-core score of 1059.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 75.64 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 8.95 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations, such as Redis SET, achieve 1.31 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 1.62 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M8-2ms offers high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for workloads requiring vast memory capacity without intensive processing demands. However, the low compute and memory bandwidth benchmarks suggest a poor performance-to-resource tradeoff for CPU-bound tasks. This server is best suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that operate within low-compute thresholds.
description: Microsoft Azure M8-2ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive workloads. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core and 219.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio. The server includes 262 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but lacks GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the bottom 10% for CPU and memory bandwidth, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1059.0 and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 8.95 GB/sec. Consequently, the M8-2ms presents a clear tradeoff: massive memory capacity paired with limited compute performance. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy, low-compute tasks, making it a suitable fit for large in-memory caching, legacy enterprise databases, and memory-bound applications that do not require high CPU throughput.
